boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations immediately beside Tulane’s Uptown campus corridors, each with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Audubon Park
cards.subtitle: Magazine Street corridor, across St. Charles Avenue from Tulane
cards.notes: Enter from St. Charles Avenue and follow the marked 1.8-mile jogging path for a shaded loop beside the lagoon.
cards.short_summary: A public park with a documented paved 1.8-mile loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon Park is open to the public and includes a 1.8-mile jogging path, lagoon, picnic pavilions, and playgrounds.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 5 AM–10 PM, according to Audubon Nature Institute.

cards.title: St. Charles Avenue Entrance
cards.subtitle: St. Charles Avenue corridor at Audubon Park
cards.notes: Use this formal Audubon Park entrance as a recognizable starting point before walking into the park from campus.
cards.short_summary: A named live-oak-lined entry into Audubon Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon identifies the St. Charles Avenue Entrance as a grand, recognizable park entrance lined with live oaks.
cards.source_title: Other Audubon Park Venues | Audubon Nature Institute
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park entrance; check park rules before planning a gathering.

cards.title: St. Charles Avenue Playground
cards.subtitle: St. Charles Avenue corridor at Exposition Boulevard
cards.notes: Find the playground near Exposition Boulevard and Pavilion 11; use the accessible park pathways to reach it.
cards.short_summary: A named playground beneath Audubon Park’s oaks.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon locates St. Charles Avenue Playground at St. Charles Avenue and Exposition Boulevard, with swings, a climbing tower, slides, and a log tunnel.
cards.source_title: Audubon Playgrounds & Family Outdoor Fun | Audubon Nature Institute
cards.access_notes: Designed for ages 2–12; accessible pathways and free street parking are listed.

cards.title: Audubon Riverview Park
cards.subtitle: Magazine Street and River Road corridor, beside Audubon Park
cards.notes: Bring a picnic or use the running paths and fields during posted park hours; follow Audubon’s park rules on site.
cards.short_summary: The riverfront portion of Audubon Park, also called The Fly.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon Riverview Park, also known as The Fly, has running paths, soccer and baseball fields, parking lots, restrooms, and views of the Mississippi River.
cards.source_title: Audubon Riverview Park | Audubon Nature Institute
cards.access_notes: Open daily 5 AM–10 PM, according to Audubon Nature Institute.

cards.title: Audubon Zoo
cards.subtitle: Magazine Street corridor at Audubon Park
cards.notes: Plan for daytime entry and check the zoo’s current exhibit notices before buying tickets or setting out across the park.
cards.short_summary: A nearby zoo with Louisiana Swamp habitat and white alligators.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon Zoo lists its address as 6500 Magazine Street and highlights the Louisiana Swamp habitat and white alligators.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are daily 10 AM–5 PM; last ticket is sold at 4 PM.

cards.title: St Charles at Tulane/Loyola Stop
cards.subtitle: St. Charles Avenue corridor, at Tulane and Loyola
cards.notes: Use this named streetcar stop as the transit-facing arrival point for Audubon Park and the Magazine Street side of the park.
cards.short_summary: A documented streetcar stop directly in front of Audubon Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Audubon states that the St. Charles Avenue streetcar stops at “St Charles at Tulane/Loyola,” in front of Audubon Park across from Tulane and Loyola.
cards.access_notes: Confirm live service and fares with the transit agency before travel.

cards.entity_name: Loyola University New Orleans Main Campus
cards.title: Loyola’s Main Campus
cards.subtitle: St. Charles Avenue corridor, beside Tulane
cards.notes: Walk the public-facing St. Charles Avenue edge and consult Loyola’s visitor information before entering campus buildings or attending events.
cards.short_summary: Tulane’s neighboring university campus across Audubon Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola says its 24-acre campus is on St. Charles Avenue and directly across from Audubon Park and Audubon Zoo.
cards.source_title: University Facts | Loyola University New Orleans
cards.access_notes: Building access and events vary; follow Loyola visitor guidance.

cards.title: The Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Freret Street corridor at 7102 Freret Street
cards.notes: Check the café’s current schedule, then visit for a donation-based drink or a listed student-club, workshop, yoga, or music event.
cards.short_summary: A Freret Street café and event space supported by NOLA Wesley.
cards.evidence_claim: NOLA Wesley identifies The Labyrinth at 7102 Freret Street as a donation-based café and a venue for student clubs, workshops, yoga, discussions, and music.
cards.access_notes: Event access and café availability vary; verify the current calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Tulane Hillel
cards.subtitle: Broadway Street corridor at 912 Broadway Street
cards.notes: Consult Tulane Hillel’s program calendar before visiting; use the Broadway Street address when planning the walk from campus.
cards.short_summary: A named Jewish campus-ministry destination on Broadway Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s student-ministry resource lists Hillel New Orleans, Jewish Campus Ministry, at 912 Broadway Street and directs readers to tulanehillel.org.
cards.source_title: Loyola University New Orleans Ministry Brochure
cards.access_notes: Programs and visitor access vary; verify directly with Tulane Hillel.

cards.title: Goldring/Woldenberg Business Complex
cards.subtitle: Freret Street corridor at McAlister Drive, beside the campus edge
cards.notes: Find the complex from the Freret Street corner and arrange any building visit through the Freeman School or campus visitor guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus-edge destination opposite the Lavin-Bernick Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Tulane identifies Goldring/Woldenberg Business Complex at 7 McAlister Drive as the second building from the Freret Street corner, across from the Lavin-Bernick Center.
cards.source_title: Contact Freeman | A. B. Freeman School of Business
cards.access_notes: Visitors must follow Tulane campus guidelines; the adjacent McAlister segment is pedestrian-only.
